Change c0497. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. VII; 1831 Ch. XXIV.

Context before (unchanged): I quickly destroyed part of my sledge to construct oars; and by these means was enabled, with infinite fatigue, to move my ice-raft in the direction of your ship.

1818 text: I had determined, if you were going southward, still to trust myself to the mercy of the seas, rather than abandon my purpose. I hoped to induce you to grant me a boat with which I could still pursue my enemy.

1831 text: I had determined, if you were going southward, still to trust myself to the mercy of the seas rather than abandon my purpose. I hoped to induce you to grant me a boat with which I could pursue my enemy.

Diff: I had determined, if you were going southward, still to trust myself to the mercy of the seas [-,-] rather than abandon my purpose. I hoped to induce you to grant me a boat with which I could [-still-] pursue my enemy.

Context after (unchanged): But your direction was northward.

result.rationale: Removes a comma before 'rather' and the adverb 'still' before 'pursue my enemy'; these are minor stylistic tightenings with no change to meaning, though 'still' slightly weakens the sense of continuing pursuit.
